title: The Broken Game
tagline: A game has gone out to players and four things in it do not work. Today you find all four and fix them.
objectives: I can read someone else's code and work out what it's supposed to do.
I can find a bug by testing, predicting and checking — not guessing randomly.
I can explain in my own words what was wrong and how I fixed it.

config.headline: Every game goes on sale with bugs in it.
lines: Today you are **QA**, the bug-finding team.

images.alt: The 1947 Harvard Mark II logbook page with the actual moth taped onto it
images.caption: First bug: a moth, 1947. US Navy, public domain.

config.help: This card is only for reading. In 1947, engineers found a real moth stuck inside a computer. Ever since, a BUG has meant a mistake in a program. QA means Quality Assurance: checking a game works before players get it. Last night, OLS GAMES released Shark Attack, and players found four bugs. Each complaint is called a TICKET. Today you read the code, test it and fix each bug. When the writing finishes, press the button at the bottom.
config.job: Read what today is about, then click Open the Case Board.
showMe: Read the words as they appear.

handbook.title: Reading Someone Else's Code
handbook.fallback: If the film won't load, don't worry — your teacher's demonstration covers everything it shows, and the cards on this screen walk you through the rest.

cases.name: The Frozen Shark
cases.ticket: My shark won’t swim RIGHT. Left, up, down all work. One star.
cases.symptom: Click the green flag. Press the RIGHT arrow. Then try the other three arrows.
cases.look: Open the Shark’s scripts. What do all the WORKING arrow scripts have on top?
cases.logHint: The right-arrow script had no… so I…
cases.replay: Click the flag. Swim a full lap, using all four arrows.
cases.replayConfirm: Full lap swum — all four arrows work

clue.free: Re-read the ticket. Which arrows work? Which ONE doesn’t? That tells you which script to check. Can’t see every stack? Click the minus (–) button at the bottom right of the code area.
clue.consult: Ask another agency — another detective pair — that has CLOSED Case 01. One question, detective to detective. (Your teacher also solved this one at the front.)
clue.consultSolo: No other agencies are on shift today — you are the whole QA team. If re-reading the ticket didn’t crack it, go straight to HQ’s clue below.
clue.hq: The bug lives on the SHARK. Compare the very TOP of each arrow script.

mechanicSteps: The top block of a stack is a HAT BLOCK.
It has a curved top. With no hat, nothing runs.
Click Events (yellow) and find ‘when space key pressed’.
Drag it onto the right-arrow stack until it snaps on.
Click ‘space’ on the new hat and pick ‘right arrow’.

img.alt: A screenshot of the game: the shark pressed hard against the right-hand wall of the tank, with a fish swimming nearby.
img.caption: FinnTastic_11’s screenshot: the shark stuck at the wall.

cases.name: The Broken Scoreboard
cases.ticket: I can HEAR the bite, but the score sits on 0. It’s eating my points!
cases.symptom: Click the green flag. Steer the shark onto the fish. Listen for the bite, then check the score.
cases.look: Find the script that runs when the fish is eaten. Which NUMBER is wrong?
cases.logHint: The change-score block said… so I…
cases.replay: Three times: click the flag, eat the fish, check the score is 1.
cases.replayConfirm: Three restarts, a clean point every time — the scoreboard tells the truth

clue.free: Re-read the ticket. The bite HAPPENS: the sound plays and the fish vanishes. So the eating works. What is the one thing that never moves?
clue.consult: Ask an agency that has CLOSED Case 02 — one question only, detective to detective. Nobody near you has closed it yet? Go straight to HQ’s clue below.
clue.consultSolo: No other agencies are on shift today — you are the whole QA team. If re-reading the ticket didn’t crack it, go straight to HQ’s clue below.
clue.hq: The bug lives on the FISH. Look in the ‘when I start as a clone’ script.

img.alt: A screenshot of the game: the shark chasing a fish, with the score display in the corner still reading 0.
img.caption: ChompChamp07’s screenshot: the score stuck on 0.

mechanicSteps: You will meet new blocks, like glide. That is normal.
Read the stack out loud, one block at a time.
Skip any block whose job is not the score.
To fix a number: click its white oval and type.
Press Enter. A number fix never moves a block.

cases.name: The Vanishing Fish
cases.ticket: One fish. ONE. I ate it, then swam round an empty ocean. Where did they GO?
cases.symptom: Click the green flag and eat the first fish. Keep playing while you count to ten. Do new fish arrive?
cases.look: Find the script that makes each new fish (a CLONE). How many does it make?
cases.logHint: The fish-maker script only ran… so I…
cases.replay: Click the flag and play for twenty seconds. Count five new fish.
cases.replayConfirm: Fish kept coming the whole time

clue.free: Re-read the ticket. The FIRST fish was fine. The fish after it never show up. Which script's whole job is making fish? Every swimming fish is a copy of the Fish in the sprite list.
clue.consult: Ask an agency — another detective pair — that has already CLOSED Case 03. One question, so make it a good one. Nobody in the room has closed it yet? Skip this step and go straight to HQ’s clue below.
clue.consultSolo: No other agencies are on shift today — you are the whole QA team. If re-reading the ticket didn’t crack it, go straight to HQ’s clue below.
clue.hq: The bug lives on the FISH. It is in the ‘when green flag clicked’ script, not the clone one.

mechanicSteps: Keep the hide block on top — it belongs there.
Drag the blocks inside repeat out to empty space.
Drag the empty repeat onto the block list. It disappears.
Drop a forever block under the hide block.
Drag your blocks back INSIDE the forever block’s mouth.
A white shadow line shows where they will land.

img.alt: A screenshot of the game: the whole tank of water with the shark alone in it and no fish anywhere.
img.caption: SharkSnackSara's screenshot: the whole ocean, empty.

cases.name: The White Void
cases.ticket: Every time I start, the screen is WHITE. The sea strolls in late!
cases.symptom: Click the green flag and watch ONLY the very first second. Then click it again. And again. Does the same wrong thing happen every time?
cases.look: This bug lives on the STAGE. Click the Stage panel, far right. What shows first?
cases.logHint: The script switched to… before… so I…
cases.replay: Click the flag three times. The ocean must be there instantly.

clue.free: Re-read the ticket. The sea is not missing — it ‘strolls in late’. So it does arrive. Watch the very first second again and say exactly what you see, in order.
clue.consult: Ask an agency that has CLOSED Case 04 — one question, detective to detective. First pair to reach it? Take HQ’s clue below — no shame in it.
clue.consultSolo: No other agencies are on shift today — you are the whole QA team. If re-reading the ticket didn’t crack it, go straight to HQ’s clue below.
clue.hq: The first switch block shows ‘backdrop1’: a blank white screen.

mechanicSteps: To change a backdrop, click the switch block’s white arrow.
Pick from the list, like Case 01’s key menu.
To delete a block, drag it onto the blocks list.
Careful: dragging a block lifts every block UNDER it too.
Put back the blocks you want to keep.

img.alt: A screenshot of the game: a plain white screen with the fish and the shark swimming on it, no ocean background.
img.caption: OceanOlivia's screenshot: fish swimming on a white screen.

stretchCase.name: The Jellyfish Job
stretchCase.ticket: Five stars! But NOTHING can hurt you. Add something to dodge.
stretchCase.job: Click ‘Choose a Sprite’ and search ‘Jellyfish’. Build the blocks in the picture. Want more? Add your own change, like a speed-up.
stretchCase.test: Dodge it, then swim into it. The game should freeze.
stretchCase.confirm: Danger installed — touching the jellyfish ends the game
stretchCase.ask: Release note: what did you add? What does it do?
stretchCase.notePlaceholder: I added a jellyfish that... so now the player...

config.stretchNudge: Your fixed game has gone back to the players — but one five-star request is still pinned to the board. Take the job, or finish for today?

rc.title: The whole-game check
rc.text: Play the WHOLE game for a minute. Watch all four fixes:
watch: All four arrows — swim a full lap.
Eat five fish — the score counts every one.
Fish keep arriving for the whole minute.
Restart twice — the ocean shows from the first instant.
rc.confirm: Full sixty-second run — every fix held
rc.ask: How many fish did you catch?

config.help: The board is your home screen. Start with Evidence Intake: it gives you the broken game. A sprite is one character or thing in the game, like the Shark. Click a sprite to see its scripts. Its SCRIPTS are the stacks of blocks that tell it what to do. A CLONE is a temporary copy of a sprite, made while the game runs. Then open the TRAINING case. The other three cases open after it, in any order. Every case: see the bug, read the code, fix one thing, log it, re-play. Your case log is one sentence: what was wrong and what you changed. A written log and a ticked re-play close the case. Stuck on a case? Open the help steps on the card. The first help steps are free. The last clue from HQ, the company’s head office, turns your stamp silver. A silver case still counts. The website cannot see inside Scratch, so only tick what you saw. The release desk sends the fixed game back to the players. Chapter 3 of the film is worth watching again.
introSteps: Play the game and SEE the bug.
Read the code. Find the ONE wrong thing.
Fix that one thing in Scratch.
Write your CASE LOG: one sentence saying what was wrong.
Play again. Tick only if you SAW it work.
config.logLead: Fix it in Scratch. Then write your case log below: **what was wrong** and **what you changed**.
config.proofNote: Only tick if you saw it work.
config.nudgeShort: Your log needs both halves in one sentence: what was wrong, and what you changed.
config.nudgeOwnWords: Say it in your OWN words — the grey line in the box is only a starter.
config.clueStep2Head: Help step 2 — ask another agency (another detective pair)
config.clueHqButton: Help step 3 — show HQ's clue (this case will then stamp SILVER instead of GOLD)
config.clueSilverNote: You took HQ's clue, so this case stamps SILVER when it closes. A silver case still counts — solve the next one without the clue for GOLD.
config.handbookNote: Come back to this film any time. Chapter 3 helps most while you are working on a case.

config.clueLadderCost: These help steps are FREE — your gold stamp is safe. Only step 3, HQ’s clue, turns this case’s stamp from GOLD to SILVER.

config.intro: They are marked. Your teacher sees your answers, so answer on your own.

items.stem: A sprite's script never runs when the green flag is clicked. What's the MOST likely reason?
options: There's no green-flag hat block on that script
The code is at the bottom of the workspace

items.stem: Your partner says: 'Fixed it! I saw one fish get eaten and the score moved.' What does a real QA tester do next?
options: Stamp it CASE CLOSED — it worked once
Re-play it and watch the fix work at least three times before closing the case
Delete the whole script and rebuild it, just to be safe
Add a few extra blocks so it definitely works

config.help: Two marked questions, answered on your own. You find out how you did at the end, after the last screen.
config.job: Answer two marked questions on your own.
showMe: Click the answer you think is right.
Click Next. On the last question, click Finish.

config.intro: Last one: five real blocks. Two are new: hide makes the sprite invisible, show makes it visible.

item.prompt: When the flag is clicked, the sprite gets into position without the player seeing it move, then appears in the middle of the screen and animates by changing costume forever.

config.help: Click blocks from the tray into your program, in the order the sentence says. Hide makes the sprite invisible. Show makes it visible again. Check when you are sure. If the order is wrong, you are shown the working order.
config.doneText: Correct — that program does exactly what the card asked.
config.job: Put five blocks in the order the sentence describes.
showMe: Click each block in the order the sentence says.
Click Check my program when you are sure.
